correctness.rationale: From the exact sphere geometry and energy conservation, inner scale b=(rho*c/g)^(a/(a-1)) reduces the hitting-time integral to sqrt(rho/g) times a positive normalized integral. Its difference from an exact asinh logarithm is uniformly bounded by an integrable error y^((a-1)/a-1)+s^2*y^(2/a-1). The outer integral differs from the point-particle travel-time integral by O(sqrt(rho/g)); inverse monotone hitting times yield each delayed branch. The normal reaction remains positive locally. Finite checks: 174 assertions for 3 exponents, 2 delays, 3 radii and geometry/contact comparisons, not used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 initiating paper establishes the radius-dependent offset geometry and exact-rest no-departure classification, not the new positive-speed uniform matched asymptotic and full deterministic selection map. A 2021 full-text Norton-dome paper models hyperfinite-grid initial-condition probabilities, not finite-radius contact geometry; a 2020 full-text RG study concerns a stochastic regularization of a first-order non-Lipschitz ODE. Actual published-finding corpus searches found no matching claim; absence of a match is not proof of uniqueness. A thematic Fletcher source was not read in full; possible implicit equivalent remains a disclosed priority risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent launch-time theorem may be implicit in older singular-regularization or physical-approximation literature, including uninspected full text of Fletcher.
Search coverage and inaccessible primary full text do not establish universal priority; this PASS is qualified best-knowledge noncoverage based on direct statement-and-implication comparisons.
All finite-parameter testing is numerical; the analytic proof, not those tests, is required for a continuous parameter theorem.

value.rationale: The initiating 2026 paper distinguishes fixed-radius uniqueness from instability and leaves the joint small-radius/launch asymptotic unquantified. This theorem resolves the natural singular-limit selection question by providing a uniform travel-time estimate for all scaled positive speeds, sharp exponential velocity control over every delay, and a separate stationary limit, a structural physical effect rather than an arbitrary specialization or a recomputation of the known exact-rest divergence.
